newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former French Lebanon hostage dies of cancer.
newsitem.headline: Former French Lebanon hostage dies of cancer.

text.p: French diplomat Marcel Fontaine, who was held hostage by Lebanese Shi'ite guerrillas for more than three years in the mid-1980s, has died of lung cancer in Paris, diplomats said on Tuesday. He was 54.

While serving as vice-consul in Beirut, he was kidnapped on March 22, 1985, by pro-Iranian Islamic Jihad gunmen and released together with two other French hostages on May 4, 1988 after long negotiations. The hostages were chained, beaten, fed poorly and subjected to mock executions.
A father of three, Fontaine went on to serve as a diplomat in Australia and Madagascar before joining the foreign ministry's protocol service in Paris five years ago.
